0.long_answer: Addison's disease is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the insufficient production of cortisol and aldosterone due to the destruction of the adrenal cortex. This deficiency disrupts the regulation of blood pressure and electrolyte balance, which can result in life-threatening hypotension if not properly managed. In Addison's disease, the immune system mistakenly attacks the adrenal glands, leading to what is known as autoimmune adrenalitis.
